from: chapitre 1 de la vidéo longue (cascade du billet de 100 $ ; coupé : « Put the two together… » et « After interest and taxes… »)
paragraphs: Now follow {one hundred dollars|$100} spent at the checkout.
About {eighty-nine dollars|$89} go straight back to the companies that made the goods. That's what Costco paid for the merchandise.
Another {nine dollars and fifteen cents|$9.15} pay for running everything else: wages, warehouses, electricity, card fees, head office.
What's left from the sale itself: {one dollar and ninety-four cents|$1.94}.
Now add the membership. For every {hundred dollars|$100} of sales, members also pay Costco about {two dollars|$2} in fees. And unlike a sale, a fee doesn't come with any goods to pay for.

Over the whole year, that's {eleven point seven billion dollars|$11.7 billion} of operating profit. Roughly half came from what's on the shelves. The other half came from the card. Full story on the channel.
